minutes.headline: Board voted to euthanize two dangerous dogs, laid out Butterfly Lane, and approved small old primary repairs.
minutes.summary: The board held a Butterfly Lane layout hearing and ratified two police officer appointments. It finished the dangerous dog hearing with a split vote on the two dogs. It heard the town manager's report on the missed marijuana ballot questions and voted recommendations on special town meeting articles. It approved small repairs at the old primary school and discussed public comment and social media policies.

public_comment.topic: A resident disputed claims about the old primary school roof, mold and brick mortar, and urged approval of the roughly eleven thousand dollar weatherproofing.
A resident criticized the animal control officer's original inspection of the kennel fence.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to order the two dangerous dogs humanely euthanized; the vote was split, with at least one member opposed.
The board voted to lay out Butterfly Lane as a public way; only Town Meeting can accept the road, so the layout goes to the special town meeting.

The board recommended two special town meeting articles, deferred two others to the meeting itself, and moved the street light LED article and the 635 Mass Ave land purchase article to annual Town Meeting.
The board authorized listed repairs at the old primary school, excluding the roof.
The board agreed in principle to adopt four of the public comment guidelines and will draft a final policy; the social media policy vote was not audible in the captions.

why_it_matters: The special town meeting warrant is taking shape: some items were recommended, some deferred, and some pushed to annual Town Meeting, so residents who vote there will see a changed list of articles.
The old primary school repairs exclude the roof, so the building's longer-term condition and cost remain an open question for the town budget, mostly taxes.
watch_next: The special town meeting, where Town Meeting must vote on accepting Butterfly Lane and on the sewer enterprise fund correction article the board deferred.
The board's draft final public comment policy.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary:
The records agree on most votes: Butterfly Lane, the police ratification, the 250 Howard refusal, and the Article 1 and 3 recommendations. They differ on several outcomes and labels.
The main point is that the dog vote tally is garbled in the captions (the official says 3-1 with Adams opposed), and the official records removing the 635 Mass Ave article where ours says it was deferred.
